reasoning_summary: The previous best setting used very small neighborhoods and distance weighting, which likely contributed to overfitting and instability on a tiny dataset. This grid broadens neighborhood sizes toward more regularized KNN settings while still including a few small-k options for comparison. It also tests both weighting schemes and both Minkowski norms, plus the equivalent Euclidean/Manhattan metric choices, to identify a more stable configuration without exceeding the candidate budget.
search_strategy: Prioritize larger n_neighbors values to reduce variance, while retaining a limited set of small and medium k values for coverage. Use a compact grid over weights, p, and metric that stays within the allowed parameter space and keeps total combinations near the target budget.
expected_effect_on_overfitting: Likely to reduce overfitting by allowing larger neighborhoods and uniform weighting, which smooth predictions and lower sensitivity to individual training points.
expected_effect_on_underfitting: May slightly increase underfitting for very large n_neighbors, but the inclusion of smaller k values should preserve the ability to recover a more flexible model if needed.
computational_cost_estimate: 120 candidates total (20 n_neighbors x 2 weights x 2 p x 3 metrics), which is at the requested upper bound and feasible for a small dataset.
warnings: For euclidean and manhattan metrics, p is ignored by sklearn but included here to satisfy the allowed search space.
The dataset is very small (n_train=21), so CV variance may remain high even after tuning.
If instability persists, consider narrowing the search around the best-performing neighborhood sizes from this grid.
